problem: Users had to visit profiles to see updates, and Facebook wanted a central stream.
title: Facebook launches News Feed, faces a user revolt, and adds privacy controls
context: Facebook introduced News Feed and Mini Feed, which broadcast friends' profile changes to each user.
decision_made: Launch News Feed to all users.
action_taken: After protests, Zuckerberg posted "Calm down. Breathe. We hear you" and added controls to limit what was shared.
observed_outcome: A group against News Feed grew to nearly 100,000 members in a day. A planned boycott and protest were called off on 8 September once privacy safeguards were added, and the features stayed.
lessons: A feature can be kept despite loud backlash if the company adds controls that address the main concern.
limitations: Only the first days were checked. Long-term growth effects were not documented in the sources used.

claims.claim_text: Facebook launched News Feed and Mini Feed on 5 September 2006.
Facebook added controls to limit sharing and the planned boycott and protest were called off on 8 September.
